Data Center market-platform revenue of 15,005M out of 26,974M total, up 41%. It includes non-AI data-center compute and networking; other market platforms are excluded.

Data Center market-platform revenue of 47,525M out of 60,922M total, up 217%, led by generative AI demand. The MD&A estimates about 40% of Data Center was AI inference, which is a split within the line, not an AI share of revenue. The line includes some non-AI servers.

Data Center market-platform revenue of 115,186M out of 130,497M total, up 142%, driven by Hopper for LLMs and generative AI and by Ethernet for AI networking. The line includes some non-AI data-center sales.

Data Center market-platform revenue of 193,737M out of 215,938M total, up 68%. This is the market line, not the 193,479M Compute & Networking segment, which includes automotive and ProViz. The line includes some non-AI data-center sales.

Management cited $1 trillion of Blackwell and Rubin revenue from 2025 through calendar 2027, which is multi-year and not a fiscal-year figure. It also cited visibility to nearly $20B of CPU revenue, a product subset rather than AI revenue. No fiscal-2027 AI revenue amount is stated.

The CFO commentary says each generation deployed at PORTS-Pike could represent about $150B to $200B of NVIDIA revenue. That is per generation, not a fiscal-year amount. The transcript expects sequential growth driven by Data Center.
